Working Title

TCAC 2.0 — Transformative Change Assessment Corpus 2.0

Code repo

Github repository

Introduction

The literature search for the Transformative Change assessment corpus was conducted using search terms provided by the experts and refined in co-operation with the IPBES task force for data and knowledge management. The search was conducted using OpenAlex, scripted from R to use the OpenAlex API. Search terms for the following searches were defined:

  • Transformative Change,
  • Nature / Environment
  • case studies and
  • additional search terms for specific corpora

To assess the quality of the corpus, sets of key papers were selected by the experts to verify if these are in the corpus. These key papers were selected per chapter / sub-chapter to ensure that the corpus is representative of each chapter.

The following terminology is used in this document:

  • Corpus: A body of works as based on a search on OpenAlex
  • Transformative Change Assessment Corpus: Short: TCA corpus; The corpus resulting from the search terms transformative AND nature
  • Case corpus: The corpus resulting from transformative AND nature AND case
  • work: terminology used for a single document in their datasewt. Each work has a unique OpenAlex id, but not necesarily a DOI.

The following searches are conducted on Title and Abstract only as the availability of fulltexts drops in 2020. OpenAlex “inherited” their initial corpus from Microsoft Academic, which contained a many fulltext articles. After that initial start, other sources were used which did not all include fulltext versions. To eliminate a bias towards fulltext articles, we limited the search to abstracts and titles only.

Results

Assessment of Search Terms Using OpenAlex

Number of Hits per Individual Corpus

Number of works returned by each individual search-term query and by the combined (nature) AND (transformative change) query, before and after the OpenAlex work-type filter is applied (only the types in input/openalex_types.csv with Included = TRUE are kept).

Show code 
cnt <- readRDS(tar_read(count_st))

# pro_request(count_only = TRUE) returns one row per query with `count`
# and `query`; the query column carries the named list element name.
labels <- c(
  tfc_complete = "Transformative Change — all types",
  tfc_filtered = "Transformative Change — filtered",
  nature_complete = "Nature — all types",
  nature_filtered = "Nature — filtered",
  tca_complete = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — all types",
  tca_filtered = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — filtered"
)

dplyr::tibble(
  search = labels[as.character(cnt$query)],
  count = as.integer(cnt$count)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Number of works matching each search on OpenAlex. *filtered* applies the work-type filter; *all types* does not."
  )
Number of works matching each search on OpenAlex. filtered applies the work-type filter; all types does not.

TCA Corpus properties

Works per type

Per OpenAlex type, work count in each corpus and the difference (TCAC 2.0 minus TCAC 1.0). Sorted by TCAC 2.0 count. Negative diff (works lost) shown in red; positive (works gained) in green.

Show code 
cmp$type_counts |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff = ifelse(
      diff < 0,
      sprintf(
        "<span style='color:red'>%s</span>",
        format(diff, big.mark = ",")
      ),
      sprintf(
        "<span style='color:green'>+%s</span>",
        format(diff, big.mark = ",")
      )
    ),
    `tcac_1.0` = format(`tcac_1.0`, big.mark = ","),
    `tcac_2.0` = format(`tcac_2.0`, big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = "Works per type in each corpus."
  )

Key papers in the corpus

Does the corpus actually cover the works the experts consider key? For each keypaper we check whether its OpenAlex id is present in TCAC 1.0 and / or in the new TCAC 2.0 extract.

Summary

Show code 
kp <- cmp$keypaper_presence
n_kp <- nrow(kp)
tibble::tibble(
  status = c("in corpus", "missing from corpus", "total keypapers"),
  `TCAC 1.0` = c(sum(kp$in_tcac10), sum(!kp$in_tcac10), n_kp),
  `% 1.0` = round(100 * c(mean(kp$in_tcac10), mean(!kp$in_tcac10), 1), 2),
  `TCAC 2.0` = c(sum(kp$in_tcac20), sum(!kp$in_tcac20), n_kp),
  `% 2.0` = round(100 * c(mean(kp$in_tcac20), mean(!kp$in_tcac20), 1), 2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Coverage of the keypaper set by each corpus."
  )
Coverage of the keypaper set by each corpus.

Detail

Per-keypaper presence in TCAC 1.0 and TCAC 2.0. Sorted with “in both” rows at the top, then by citation. Rows flagged red are missing from that corpus — candidates for revisiting the search terms (or the keypaper itself, if it’s borderline off-topic).

Show code 
cmp$keypaper_presence |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `TCAC 1.0` = ifelse(
      in_tcac10,
      "<span style='color:green'>✓</span>",
      "<span style='color:red'>✗</span>"
    ),
    `TCAC 2.0` = ifelse(
      in_tcac20,
      "<span style='color:green'>✓</span>",
      "<span style='color:red'>✗</span>"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    `TCAC 1.0`,
    `TCAC 2.0`,
    citation,
    title
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Keypaper presence in each corpus."
  )

Publications over time

Bars: yearly count of works in the TCAC 2.0 corpus. Red line: cumulative proportion of the corpus. Blue line: cumulative proportion of all of OpenAlex over the same year range — a useful baseline for “is the corpus skewing recent vs the literature as a whole?”. Both cumulative lines use the secondary (right-hand) axis.

Show code 
years <- arrow::open_dataset(tar_read(corpus_tcac20)) |>
  dplyr::count(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(publication_year), publication_year >= 1900) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p = n / sum(n),
    p_cum = cumsum(p)
  )

# OpenAlex universe baseline (from yearly_counts target, label =
# "openalex_universe"). Recompute its cumulative proportion over the
# same year window as the corpus so the two lines are comparable.
oa_universe <- readRDS(tar_read(yearly_counts)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    label == "openalex_universe",
    publication_year %in% years$publication_year
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_oa = count / sum(count),
    p_oa_cum = cumsum(p_oa)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(publication_year, p_oa, p_oa_cum)

ymax <- max(years$n)

ggplot2::ggplot(years, ggplot2::aes(x = publication_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = n), fill = "#BBBBBB") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    ggplot2::aes(y = p_cum * ymax),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = oa_universe,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = p_oa_cum * ymax),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of works per year (bars)",
    sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(
      ~ . / ymax,
      name = "Cumulative proportion (red = corpus, blue = OpenAlex universe)"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Publication year") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

Added, removed, kept (vs TCAC 1.0)

Per-year change in corpus composition between the two extracts. Added (green, above zero) = works present in TCAC 2.0 but not in TCAC 1.0. Removed (red, below zero, drawn as negative counts so the visual is symmetric) = works present in TCAC 1.0 but not in TCAC 2.0. Both (grey backdrop) = works present in both — included to show the scale of the carried-over base, not the change.

Show code 
ys <- cmp$yearly_status |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = status,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0L
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    removed = `removed (only in TCAC 1.0)`,
    both = `both`,
    added = `added (only in TCAC 2.0)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(removed_neg = -removed)

ggplot2::ggplot(ys, ggplot2::aes(x = publication_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = both, fill = "both"),
    width = 1,
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = added, fill = "added (only in TCAC 2.0)"),
    width = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = removed_neg, fill = "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)"),
    width = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    breaks = c(
      "added (only in TCAC 2.0)",
      "both",
      "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)"
    ),
    values = c(
      "added (only in TCAC 2.0)" = "#59A14F",
      "both" = "#999999",
      "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)" = "#E15759"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) format(abs(x), big.mark = ",")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Publication year",
    y = "Number of works"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
Show code 
cmp$yearly_status |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = sum(n), .by = status) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`%` = round(100 * n / sum(n), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = sprintf(
      "Aggregate composition of the corpus change. TCAC 1.0: %s works; TCAC 2.0: %s works.",
      format(cmp$n_tcac10, big.mark = ","),
      format(cmp$n_tcac20, big.mark = ",")
    )
  )
